title: Wireframe Design Review Input
description: What is to be wireframed and why: the use (design of a new or changed surface, or as-is drawing of an existing visualiser), the surface, and where the drawings are kept. Called from Process_CRDM_Requirements (Call_Wireframe) for Design use, when a requirement changes a rendered surface.

use.description: `design`: a new or changed UI, at least two candidates compared blind. `as-is`: an existing visualiser drawn as it renders on main, exactly one candidate.

topic.description: Kebab-case name of what is drawn. For Design use from CRDM it is the proposal slug, so the drawings sit beside docs/proposals/<topic>.md; for as-is use it is the docs/wireframes/<topic>/ directory name.

surface.description: The rendered surface: a page, a visualiser ref, the navbar, a form, an app screen.

intent.description: Who the screen is for, what they need to do, and what it must show. Absent: written in step 1 (from the requirements for Design use; read off the visualiser's declaration for as-is use).

requirements.description: Design use from CRDM: the requirement keys or sentences that change this surface, verbatim.

proposal.description: Design use from CRDM: repository-relative path of the request's proposal (docs/proposals/<slug>.md), whose assets the candidates become.

humanReviewer.description: Who chooses between candidates. From CRDM: the requester or the BA, by GitHub handle.

kind.description: The Tool the request for feedback goes through.

url.description: The issue or pull request; absent for the conversation.

channels.description: Where the candidates are shown: where the requester will look, chosen from context, and more than one may be right (staging-review, the deep-link rule, point 5). Each carries the same staging deep links and screenshots.

branch.description: The feature branch the candidates are committed on, so feature-staging publishes them.
